## About

I am a PhD student in mathematics at **National Taiwan University**, advised by **Professor Hui-Wen Lin**. My research interests include algebraic geometry, toric varieties, and Gromov–Witten theory.

I received my B.S. in Mathematics from National Taiwan University in 2024 and began my PhD studies in the same year.

::: {.research-line}
<span>Research interests</span>
Algebraic geometry · Toric varieties · Gromov–Witten theory 
:::

## Selected work

::: {.work-item}
<span class="work-year">2026 · PREPRINT</span>

### Quantum invariance under non-smooth toric flops of the simplest type

With Jia-Hua Chong and Hui-Wen Lin. 

For a non-smooth toric flop of the simplest type, we provide the quantum product formulas and construct the degree-preserving quantum correspondence via generalized analytic continuation which is achieved through a regularization map. Moreover, the generating functions of Gromov--Witten invariants with ancestors are invariant for all genera.

[Abstract & links →](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24066)
:::

::: {.work-item}
<span class="work-year">2024 · Math. Z. 313 (2026), no.3, Paper No.46</span>

### Fiber products under toric flops and flips

With Hui-Wen Lin and Sz-Sheng Wang.

Let $\Sigma$ and $\Sigma'$ be two refinements of a fan $\Sigma_0$ and $f \colon X_{\Sigma} \dashrightarrow X_{\Sigma'}$ be the birational map induced by $X_{\Sigma} \rightarrow X_{\Sigma_0} \leftarrow X_{\Sigma'}$. We show that the graph closure $\Graphc$ is a \emph{not necessarily normal} toric variety and we give a combinatorial criterion for its normality.  

In contrast to it, for $f$ being a toric flop/flip, we show that the scheme-theoretic fiber product $X \coloneqq X_{\Sigma}\times_{X_{\Sigma_0}}X_{\Sigma'}$ is in general \emph{not toric}, though it is still \emph{irreducible} and $X_{\rm red} = \overline{\Gamma}_f$.  

A complete numerical criterion to ensure $X = X_{\rm red}$ is given for 3-folds, which is fulfilled when $X_\Sigma$ has at most terminal singularities. In this case, we further conclude that $X$ is normal.  

The result turns out to be a key step to study the correspondence between Chow motives under toric flops and flips.

[Abstract & links →](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.12446)
:::
